messages:
sasha (sales): FYI ACME just re-upped and their ask: per-team cost breakdown in Console + the ability to click from a row into the exact request trace. they said it's blocking their chargeback rollout.
anya (pm): thanks. do we have the exact ask? must-have vs nice-to-have?
ben (support): must-have: daily per-team cost with ability to filter by model/route and export CSV. nice-to-have: trace-link from the console to an APM trace for a given request id.
kevin (eng): linking to traces is doable but requires propagation of trace ids from the frontend to backend and including them in logs/telemetry. also an indexed field in our cost events. storage + query perf are the main concerns.
tara (design): initial UI sketch: dashboard with top-level cards (total cost, avg latency), table with team, cost, requests, pct change. drilldown row -> recent requests list with a button "open trace" that navigates to APM with trace id. CSV/export & a small permissions control.
anya (pm): proposal for scope: MVP = per-team aggregated cost (daily), filter by model/route, CSV export, RBAC to limit who can view chargeback. Trace linking = beta: supported only when x-trace-id header present and tenant has APM linked. Launch criteria: auth, basic perf (table loads <2s for 30-day view), CSV export works, unit tests + e2e.
kevin (eng): backend tasks I see: 1) emit trace_id in billing event schema, 2) add index on trace_id and owner_id, 3) query endpoints for aggregated cost + paginated request list, 4) opt-in flag for retention. estimate: backend ~6w, front ~2w, infra/ops ~1w. total ~9w.
ben (support): customer asked for rollout timeline ~Q2. is 9w realistic? they want early access if we can do canary.
anya (pm): ok set expectation: offer early access to ACME as canary for trace-link beta. MVP GA target = 9w but we'll do milestone checkpoints every 2w.
observability-bot: New event schema proposal posted: https://internal/redwood/observability/events/trace-prop-v2 (automated note)
kevin (eng): security note: we need to gate trace links behind project-level APM integration + permission check. also ensure no PII in exported CSVs.
tara (design): will mock the table and trace modal by EOD tomorrow and post in #design-review. simple column set: team, model, route, tokens, cost, requests, trace-link.
sasha (sales): ACME will join canary. I'll loop them in and get sample logs with trace ids.
anya (pm): I'll create the PRD and backlog ticket (#PRD-789). tagging eng/design/support for intake. next steps: I will post acceptance criteria + rollout plan in the ticket. :thumbsup:
kevin (eng): replied +1. will carve out time for schema change first.
ben (support): thanks — I'll add customer example payloads to the ticket.
anya (pm): assigning owners: kevin = backend, tara = UI, ben = customer validation, sasha = canary coordination. I'll update the ticket with timeline checkpoints.
sasha (sales): awesome — sending ACME the invitation to pilot now :rocket:
